questions.prompt: How many computational-basis states does a two-qubit register have?
questions.explanation: Two qubits have 2^2 = 4 basis strings: 00, 01, 10 and 11.

questions.prompt: What operation combines two separate statevectors?
questions.explanation: The tensor product pairs every amplitude from one state with every amplitude from the other.

questions.prompt: In QuantLearn's displayed order, which entry represents |10>?
questions.explanation: The order is 00, 01, 10, 11, so |10> is the third entry.
q1 is always zero, while q0 is balanced, so only 00 and 01 have amplitude.
The 10 amplitude uses q1's 1/2 and q0's 1/sqrt(2), whose squared product is 1/8.

questions.prompt: How many amplitudes does a general n-qubit pure state need?
questions.explanation: There is one amplitude for each n-bit computational-basis string.

options.text: A joint state that can be written as one state tensor another
Any state made with a two-qubit gate
A state with only one nonzero amplitude

questions.explanation: Separability means the joint vector factors into independent subsystem states.

questions.prompt: Why does reversing tensor factors cause a labeling bug?

options.text: The numeric entries can remain plausible while basis labels move
Basis order is not part of a statevector

questions.explanation: The same local values can occupy different slots when q1 and q0 order is reversed.

questions.prompt: Does a four-entry two-qubit vector automatically describe entanglement?

options.text: Yes, every four-entry vector is entangled
No, it may be a tensor product or an entangled state
No, two qubits cannot be entangled
Yes, if one amplitude is zero

questions.explanation: Dimension and entanglement are different ideas. Some four-entry vectors factor and some do not.
